Detect Equipment Problems Earlier with Condition Data

Thematic Area: Condition Monitoring & Predictive Maintenance

How might we combine equipment readings and maintenance history to identify abnormal conditions and provide useful warning before problems disrupt operations?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants to explore earlier detection of equipment problems using condition data and analytics.

The opportunity is to connect asset signals with maintenance knowledge and provide useful warnings for technicians. Relevant startups offer sensor integration, condition monitoring, time-series analysis and machine learning.

The collaboration will select assets, review sensor coverage and prepare operating data and recorded fault histories for a focused monitoring application.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Missed early warnings: Equipment issues are harder to address early without usable condition information.
  • Less informed maintenance decisions: Technicians need relevant condition evidence to prioritise inspections and repairs.
  • Alert overload: Poor-quality signals and excessive false warnings reduce the practical usefulness of monitoring tools.

Existing Efforts

  • Existing maintenance records: Maintenance logbooks provide a starting point for connecting equipment behaviour with historical service activity.
  • Available research: A university research-stage technology analyses relationships between multiple sensor signals to identify unusual operating behaviour.
  • Collaboration focus: Select assets, synchronise sensor readings and connect them with verified maintenance records. Configure and evaluate equipment-specific anomaly detection, measuring warning time, false-alert rates and usefulness to technicians. Use the findings to develop actionable inspection and maintenance responses.

Potential Market Size

  • Global predictive maintenance market: The global market is estimated at US$14.2 billion in 2025 and is forecast to reach US$98.1 billion by 2033, with 27.9% annual growth during 2026–2033. The market spans condition-based maintenance solutions and services across several industries.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
